```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

```


Get the data
```{r data}
panrgp <- "<PROJECT_ROOT>/Results/Pangenome/PPANGGOLIN/PANRGP"

rgps <- read_tsv(paste0(panrgp, "/regions_of_genomic_plasticity.tsv"),
                 show_col_types = F) %>% 
  rename("rgp_id" = "region")

spots <- read_tsv(paste0(panrgp, "/spots.tsv"), show_col_types = F)

spot_summary <- read_tsv(paste0(panrgp, "/summarize_spots.tsv"),
                         show_col_types = F) %>% 
  rename("spot_id" = "spot")
```

Clusters of the less conserved shell and cloud gene families form RGP, which primarily result from horizontal gene transfer events. To study the dynamics of RGP, these regions from different genomes can be grouped into specific insertion spots based on the presence of conserved flanking persistent genes.

```{r concept, echo=F, out.width="70%"}

# https://journals.plos.org/plosbiology/article?id=10.1371/journal.pbio.3002746#pbio.3002746.s015
knitr::include_graphics(path = '<PROJECT_ROOT>/Notebooks/ss_panrgp.png')
```



Merge both of the df
```{r merge_df}

spots_with_rgps <- rgps %>% 
  left_join(spots, by = "rgp_id") %>% 
  left_join(spot_summary, by = "spot_id")



rgps %>% 
  left_join(spots, by = "rgp_id") %>%
  ## group by
  group_by(spot_id) %>%
  summarise(n_rgp = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_rgp)) %>% 
  head() %>% 
  knitr::kable()

```
What we can see is there are around 652 unique spots in the RSSC pangenome. Lets take a closer look at spot_61
```{r spot61}
rgps %>% 
  left_join(spots, by = "rgp_id") %>%
  filter(spot_id == "spot_61") %>% 
  arrange(desc(genes)) %>% 
  filter(genome == "GMI1000") %>% 
  knitr::kable()

```

Spots can be characterised by the presence of >1 and <= 100 unique RGP families with diverse gene content, and hotspots by the presence of >100 unique RGP families.
```{r spot_char}

# 
# spot_characterization <- spots_with_rgps %>% 
#   group_by(spot_id) %>% 
#   mutate(spot_character = case_when(
#     n_distinct(rgp_id) > 100 ~ "Hotspot",
#     TRUE ~ "Spot"
#   )) %>% 
#   mutate(CONTIGS = case_when(
#     contig == "contig_1" ~ "Chromosome",
#     TRUE ~ "Plasmid"
#   ))



# Characterize each of the spots
spot_characterization <- spots_with_rgps %>% 
  
  mutate(SPOT_CHAR = ifelse(nb_unique_family_sets > 100, "Hotspot", "Spot")) %>% 
  mutate(CONTIGS = case_when(
    contig == "contig_1" ~ "Chromosome",
    TRUE ~ "Plasmid"
  )) %>% 
# NOTE: sometime panRGP marks whole contigs as a RGP,
# therefore it doesnot consider them to  include as a spot, so 
# we donot take those RGP in account.
    filter(SPOT_CHAR != "NA") 

spot_characterization %>%
  filter(spot_id == "spot_0") %>% 
  pull(contig) %>% 
  unique()
```

Hotspots are somewhat widespread accross the chromosome and in the Plasmid sequences
```{r plot_char}
# check the distribution of the spots over the contigs

# count the number of spots that are found in either chromosome and plasmid
spot_characterization %>%
  # select(SPOT_CHAR, spot_id, CONTIGS) %>% 
  group_by(CONTIGS, SPOT_CHAR) %>%
  summarise(n = n_distinct(spot_id)) %>% 
  ggplot(., aes(y = CONTIGS, x = n, fill = SPOT_CHAR)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  theme_bw()

spot_characterization %>%
  # filter(SPOT_CHAR == "Hotspot") %>% 
  pull(spot_id) %>%
  unique() %>% 
  length()
  
```

Lets take a closer look at spot_61, which is present in the contig_1 or Chromosome for most of the strains, however for only `MolK2` strain, it has been spotted in the plasmid (contig_2), and made up of `MolK2_contig_2_RGP_23`, and contains 5 genes	and it contains 108 distinct RGPs with varying number of genes in them!
